instructions:
You are the need-analysis step of an operational agent. The principal wrote one sentence. First
decide how it is handled: a request to explain, advise, brainstorm or plan something (e.g. 'how could we...',
'what should I...', 'tell me ways to...') is a conversation, answered by replying, even when it mentions the world.
Otherwise decide
whether they want to know something (information), to have an ability they will keep using (tool), or to have
something done once (action). Decide
what information (or ability) they actually need, without choosing any implementation, provider, tool,
metric source or architecture. Identify the subjects exactly as written. For each question, define the quantity
precisely enough that two engineers would count the same thing, including who must be excluded for the answer to
be true to the principal's words, and which time windows make it meaningful. State which forms of answer are
honest when an exact count is impossible. Choose the deliverable form from the wording (e.g. 'at a glance' means
a view readable in seconds that stays current). For tool and action needs list requirements: what must be
possible, each with an observable acceptance check, tied to the words it comes from; questions may then be empty.

payload.sentence: Every morning, tell me whether it's a good day to dry laundry outside in Osaka.

handled_as.description: conversation: a request to explain, advise, brainstorm, plan, compare ideas or give a how-to or an opinion -- answered by thinking it through and replying once, not by reading a live figure or keeping track of anything; software_capability: anything answered from a current fact, figure or status Regent can read, kept track of, reminded, built or done with software; housing: finding a place to live; other: only what no software can do (a physical task)

as_written.description: the exact words in the sentence

windows.description: time windows that make the answer meaningful, e.g. 24h, 7d, 30d, all_time

deliver_at_local.description: HH:MM local time if the wording implies when to be told (e.g. 'every morning')

need_type.description: information: wants to know something; tool: wants an ability they keep using (an app, a place to do X); action: wants something done once

requirements.description: for tool and action needs: what must be possible, each with an observable acceptance check

from_words.description: the words in the sentence this comes from

definitions_to_state.description: ambiguities the answer must resolve explicitly

questions.question: Is today a good day to dry laundry outside in Osaka?
questions.quantity: Verdict (yes/no) on whether today's daytime weather in Osaka favors outdoor line-drying: no rain or precipitation expected during drying hours, plus supportive conditions (low humidity, some wind/sun, comfortable temperature). Verdict is based on forecast for today's daylight drying hours.
questions.population: Today's forecast for Osaka city, during daytime drying hours (roughly 08:00-18:00 local)

questions.question: What are the key conditions behind the verdict (rain chance, humidity, wind, temperature, and any pollen/PM2.5/yellow-dust warnings)?
questions.quantity: Today's forecast precipitation probability (%), relative humidity (%), wind speed, temperature (°C), and air-quality/pollen alerts for Osaka during drying hours

deliverable.why: 'Every morning, tell me' implies a recurring short daily message with a verdict. Time of day not specified, so a morning default is used.

definitions_to_state: 'Good day' criteria: no rain expected during drying hours (e.g. precipitation probability below a stated threshold), with humidity, wind, and temperature considered
'Morning' delivery time (assumed 07:00 local, Japan Standard Time)
'Osaka' means Osaka city (not the whole prefecture)
Whether pollen, PM2.5, or yellow dust count against a good day
The forecast source and its limits: the verdict is a forecast, not certainty

rekeyed.why: need-analysis prompt gained the 'conversation' category; a live run with the new prompt classified this sentence the same way (software_capability)
